items.name: langchain4j
items.description: LangChain4j is an idiomatic, open-source Java library for building LLM-powered applications on the JVM. It offers a unified API over popular LLM providers and vector stores, and makes implementing tool calling (including MCP support), agents and RAG easy. It integrates seamlessly with enterprise Java frameworks like Quarkus and Spring Boot.

readme.excerpt:
The goal of LangChain4j is to simplify integrating LLMs into Java applications.

Here's how: 1. Unified APIs: LLM providers (like OpenAI or Google Vertex AI) and embedding (vector) stores (such as Pinecone or Milvus) use proprietary APIs. LangChain4j offers a unified API to avoid the need for learning and implementing specific APIs for each of them. To experiment with different LLMs or embedding stores, you can easily switch between them without the need to rewrite your code. LangChain4j currently supports 20+ popular LLM providers and 30+ embedding stores. 2. Comprehensive Toolbox: Since early 2023, the community has been building numerous LLM-powered applications, identifying common abstractions, patterns, and techniques. LangChain4j has refined these into practical code. Our toolbox includes tools ranging from low-level prompt templating, chat memory management, and function calling to high-level patterns like Agents and RAG. For each abstraction, we provide an interface along with multiple ready-to-use implementations based on common techniques. Whether you're building a chatbot or developing a RAG with a complete pipeline from data ingestion to retrieval, LangChain4j offers a wide variety of options. 3. Numerous Examples: These examples showcase how to begin creating various LLM-powered applications, providing inspiration and enabling you to start building quickly.

LangChain4j began development in early 2023 amid the ChatGPT hype. We noticed a lack of Java counterparts

items.description: fck_data_brokers.py is a free, open-source Python script that sends opt-out and deletion requests to data brokers on your behalf.

readme.excerpt:
"Today was funny: I was dealing with some scumbag data broker this morning, trying to get a good friend of mine's information deleted, and they WOULDN'T do it. No matter what I tried. I felt so ugh! I just wanted to reach through the screen and punch them in the face. Well, Mr. Data Broker, here's me reaching through the screen and punching you in the face. Enjoy f ck data brokers.py"

I remove people's data from data brokers. It is one of my main part-time jobs, and it has been a wild ride.

All I want to do is help people. In the world of AI that has become next to impossible. From where I sit, data brokers have ramped up production almost 1000x since GPT-4 came out. Every scraper got smarter, every profile got fatter, and every "people search" site got a hundred cousins.

Sends the letters from your own free mailbox, or hands them to you ready to send.

Chases the ones that go quiet and tells you where to file a complaint about the ones that refuse.
Python 3.8 or newer. Check with python --version . If you do not have it, get it free from python.org.
An email address. A free one is fine.
Tell it who you are. Name, email, city, and where you live. No street address, no birthday, no ID. Brokers get the minimum.

items.name: davish
items.description: Your server, as a desktop. A lightweight SSH client with an OS-like UI. Nothing to install on the server.

readme.excerpt:
A desktop for your Linux servers. Terminal, files, services, Docker, logs, cron, nginx, ports, a browser, disk, login security, SSH keys, packages and git over plain SSH, in one place that feels like an operating system. Nothing to install on the server.

- Open it and you're in. No login screen, no web panel: Davish connects to the server you used last with your SSH key and puts you on its desktop. Nothing extra listens on the server, so there is no new port to open or protect. - Agentless. Davish only needs sshd and SFTP. Everything runs from your machine over SSH; nothing is copied to, installed on or left behind on the server. - You see every command. Anything destructive (stop a service, remove a file, restart a container, replace a crontab) shows the exact command before it runs. The command log records everything Davish ran on your behalf, and exports the changes as a shell script you can read and run again. - Secrets stay in your keychain. Passwords and passphrases live only in the OS keychain. A sudo password is never saved: when root is needed, Davish asks for it once per session, keeps it in memory only, forgets it after 15 minutes unused and hands it to sudo on stdin, or you run the command in a terminal yourself. - Locks when you step away. A lock password of its own, Touch ID on macOS; it locks when the machine wakes, after idle time or with ⌘L . Sessions keep running behind the lock, but nothing reaches a server until you unlock. - Many servers, one desktop. Ea

items.description: CubePod — Persistent Writable RootFS MicroVM execution platform for AI Agents

readme.excerpt:
Documentation · Interactive API Reference · 中文 README · 中文文档 · llms.txt

CubePod is an open-source, cloud-native execution platform designed for long-lived, high-autonomy AI Agents, featuring native E2B compatibility and native Kubernetes Runtime scheduling . Part of the Open-Source CubePlex Agent Stack , CubePod provides the persistent hardware-isolated execution layer powering CubePlex (Team Agent Workspace) and CubeLoop (Async Agent Runtime), delivering MicroVM execution with instant hibernation/resume and full system-level persistence.

Modern AI agents (DevOps agents, software engineering assistants, interactive data analysts) operate with broad shell privileges: they dynamically install system packages ( apt , pip , npm , Rust/C++ compilers), launch headless or interactive GUI browsers, and interact with external APIs using privileged credentials.
features: Ephemeral RootFS (Only /workspace Persists) : Standard container sandboxes discard modifications to /usr , /etc , and /var whenever a sandbo

Network Filesystem I/O Bottleneck : Mounting NFS or CephFS across sandboxes causes catastrophic latency during npm install , pip install , o
Plaintext Secret Exposure : Injecting real API keys into container environment variables exposes credentials to untrusted LLM-generated code
rootfs-pvc : Carries the OverlayFS upperdir and workdir . Stores all delta modifications to /usr , /etc , and /var created by apt-get , pip
workspace-pvc : Mounted directly at /workspace (with 1000:1000 ownership). Preserves source code, artifacts, and skills.
Suspend : When an agent sandbox is paused or hits its idle timeout, podd executes sync + fsfreeze to flush kernel page caches and quiesce fi
Resume : Any incoming request (HTTP, command execution, or panel access) triggers cubepod-gateway to schedule a fresh MicroVM Pod on any clu

readme.excerpt:
A database client for Windows that stays smooth. GPU-rendered, written in Rust, one small exe.

Locus talks to MySQL / MariaDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Redis, Oracle and SQL Server. Results stream into the grid while the query is still running, and cancelling really stops the query on the server.

- It does not freeze. Big results stream into a virtualized grid. A slow query or a huge table does not block typing, scrolling or switching tabs. - It is careful with production. A connection marked Production is read-only by default. Writes need a timed unlock, every writing statement asks for its own confirmation, and each one lands in an audit log. The gate classifies the statement text; functions called by a SELECT are not checked for side effects, except known built-ins ( nextval , pg terminate backend , GET LOCK ...). - It stays out of your way. One window, vertical tabs, split panes, and a command palette for everything else.

items.name: xnulinux
items.description: XNU as a loadable kernel module inside Linux (macOS personality for arm64 Linux)

readme.excerpt:
Run macOS userspace on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it.

xnulinux builds XNU, the open-source kernel of macOS, from Apple's published sources and runs it as a loadable kernel module ( xnu.ko ) inside an unmodified arm64 Linux kernel. The hosted XNU drives the CPU and MMU directly, so macOS processes run natively next to Linux processes on the same CPUs, with no hypervisor between them. Linux lends XNU its memory, timers, files, network and GPU through a small interface module ( fki.ko ).

With a stock Ubuntu kernel, insmod xnu.ko boots a macOS 27 system disk made by Apple's own installer to the desktop: loginwindow, WindowServer, Dock, Finder, Safari and Chrome.

书写交互 · 空间与阅读 · 原生 Markdown · 功能全景 · 常用快捷键 · 性能 · 从源码运行 · 参与贡献 · 路线图

ArcMD 将熟悉的 Markdown 写作流带入细腻跟手的原生富文本画布。 完全使用 Go 与 MyGo Native UI 自研开发——由 Go 直接驱动窗口绘制、字形排版与系统输入， 零 HTML、JavaScript、WebView、Electron 或 cgo 。

features: 未改动段落原样保留 ：通过分块比对原始 Markdown（ ImportSource ），未编辑的段落不会改写你原有的缩进、列表符号或链接写法。
扩展排版 100% 无损往返 ：文字颜色、背景高亮、手绘标注、五色高亮块（GitHub Alert [!NOTE] 等）、折叠块（ ）、跨格合并与着色表格、自定义比例双栏（ data-widths ）以及页面图标、封面与字数目标，通过标准 Markdown + 语义化 HTML
